atoms.text: Queen Leafy lives near the Equator. Will you learn about the Equator with her?

instruction.text: Can you point out the Equator to Queen Leafy?

feedback.end: The Equator is an imaginary line stretching around the middle of Earth. It divides Earth into two halves: the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere.

instruction.text: Unlike the poles, areas around the Equator are very warm. Select the images of things you might see there.

feedback.end: The Equator passes through 13 different countries and 3 oceans.

instruction.text: Find the sun in this image to tell Queen Leafy a fun fact about the Equator.

feedback.end: Because of the curved shape of the planet, sunlight hits the Equator more directly than anywhere else on Earth. This is why areas around the Equator are so hot!

atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>What does the Equator look like?</voice>

atoms.a: “Does the Equator go around the Earth like a belt?”
